title: Graceful shutdown with signal handling and pending request draining
description: Adds built‑in support for graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM, ensuring the HTTP server stops accepting new connections while allowing in‑flight requests to finish. This improves reliability in production deployments and prevents abrupt termination of client requests.
testCases: Simulate SIGTERM signal and verify server stops accepting new connections after existing ones complete
Send multiple concurrent requests, trigger shutdown, and assert that all responses are received before the process exits
acceptance: When the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM, the framework stops accepting new requests within 100 ms, waits up to 5 seconds for active requests to finish, then exits with code 0. If requests exceed the timeout, they are force‑closed and the process exits with code 1. Logging indicates shutdown steps.
reason: Production environments require reliable termination to avoid data loss and improve uptime; adding graceful shutdown eliminates the need for external wrappers and aligns yantraverse with best‑practice Node.js server behavior.
